page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and a custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a bundled 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 24282.92 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8586.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 975.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, reaching 946.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 162.96 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The instance demonstrates average performance in database operations, with Passmark database operations scoring 10374.7 and Redis SET operations achieving 20.4 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds are generally poor to weak, particularly for prompt processing on 7B models.

The r6gd.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by combining a high memory-to-vCPU ratio with high-speed local NVMe storage on an ARM64 architecture. This resource density reduces the need for external block storage attachments for data-intensive tasks. The hardware profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require local scratch space, such as medium-sized databases, caching layers, and distributed data processing.
